text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Prospects poor for European Union reforms as EU foreign ministers gather in Netherlands; London expresses resistance
- Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) dismiss pressure to choose chancellery candidate for 1998 election, following Chancellor Helmut Kohl's decision to run again
- SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine continues to call for direct talks with Kohl on tax reform
- Framework for European monetary union put in place, sanctions for breach of criteria put in place
- Chemical industry says it has fulfilled its commitment to provide training places
HANDELSBLATT
- EU finance ministers agree drastic penalties for EMU members who exceed deficit limits
- Utilities may face tax on reserves
- No compromise in sight in government efforts to enlist opposition SPD on tax reform
- Chancellery rejects idea of cabinet reshuffle involving merger of finance and economics ministry
- Handelsblatt leading economic indicator for west Germany up 1.7 percent
- Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel slams Turkey over criticism in connection with arson attack on Turkish family in Germany
- European shipbuilders not prepared to scrap all subsidies while other global competitors continue to enjoy them
- Most retailers pessimistic about sales growth
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- EU Finance Ministers agree on stability pact and timetable for monetary union
- Politicians in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats call for "welfare detectives" to curb abuse of welfare benefits
- Utilities may face billions of marks in tax demands on reserves
- Deregulation boosts competition in haulage market
DIE WELT
- EU Finance Ministers agree on stability pact for monetary union
- Turkish Interior Minister backs off criticism of Germany in connection with arson attack on Turkish family
- Politicians in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats call for "welfare detectives" to curb abuse of welfare benefits

- Debate opens up in SPD about nomination of leading candidate for 1998 general election, as party comes under increasing pressure following Chancellor Helmut Kohl's declaration that he will stand again
- Economic prospects improve as job cuts in chemical industry come to a halt
- Waigel under pressure in cabinet to modify tax reform proposals
- President of Federal Cartel Office says plans for new law to limit power of banks do not go far enough
